title: Which Kind of Object Is It?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
Learning Objects
Interactive Simulation
Instrumented MicroSim
Classification
description: A p5.js drag-and-drop sorting activity in which learners place twelve example cards into four bins (learning object, interactive simulation, MicroSim, instrumented MicroSim) and receive feedback naming the deciding property.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish learning objects, interactive simulations, MicroSims, and instrumented MicroSims by sorting example descriptions into the correct category.
prerequisites: Definitions of the four kinds of object (Chapter 1)

accessibility.notes: Keys 1-4 place the card without dragging; feedback uses words (Correct / Not quite) as well as color

controls.label: Next / Finish / Shuffle
controls.purpose: Advance after a correct placement, finish the round, or start a new shuffled round

controls.label: Example card
controls.purpose: Drag into a bin to classify the example

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification practice with property-based corrective feedback
keyQuestions: What does an interactive simulation have that a video does not?
What makes a desktop simulator fail to be a MicroSim?
What single property turns a MicroSim into an instrumented MicroSim?
commonMisconceptions: Any interactive program is a MicroSim
A metadata record alone makes something a MicroSim
Tracking page views makes a MicroSim instrumented
assessmentOpportunities: Naming the deciding property for a missed card
